q: What are the library timings on working days?
a: On working days the libraries are open Monday to Saturday from 8.00 am to 9.00 pm.

q: Is the library open on Sunday?
a: Yes. On Sundays the library is open from 10:00 am to 6:00 pm.

q: What are the library timings during vacation?
a: During vacation the library is open Monday to Saturday from 8.00 am to 5.00 pm.

q: What is the loan period for law students in the library?
a: Law students (all levels) can borrow books for 7 days; the number of books depends on their level.

q: For how many days can PhD scholars borrow library books?
a: PhD and post-doctoral scholars have a loan period of 21 days.

q: How many times can I renew a library book?
a: A book may be renewed only once online. Renewal can be done online or through an SMS.

q: How many pages can I photocopy from a library book?
a: Photocopy and scanning are available from 9:30 am to 6:30 pm, with a maximum of 60 pages per book. Full book copying is not permitted.

q: How long can I book a symposium hall in the library?
a: Symposium halls can be reserved at the circulation desk for a maximum of 1 hour per booking.

q: Where can I find previous years' question papers?
a: Previous years' question papers are accessible to all registered students at https://databank.christuniversity.in/out.php.

q: How do I access e-resources from outside the campus?
a: All e-resources are IP-based on campus. Remote access is also available: login details are sent to your registered email, and everything is accessed through KNIMBUS.

q: Can I use my mobile phone in the library?
a: No. Use of a mobile phone is prohibited in the library, and strict silence must be maintained.

q: When was the Bannerghatta Road Campus established?
a: The Bangalore Bannerghatta Road Campus was established in 2016.

q: When was the Yeshwanthpur Campus started?
a: The Bangalore Yeshwanthpur Campus was established in 2022.

q: When was the Delhi NCR campus established?
a: The Delhi NCR Campus in Ghaziabad was established in 2013.

q: What is the NAAC accreditation grade of the university?
a: CHRIST (Deemed to be University) is currently accredited with an 'A+' grade by NAAC.

q: Who founded the vision behind CHRIST University?
a: The University was born out of the educational vision of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, who founded the CMI congregation that administers the University.

q: When did Christ College become a Deemed to be University?
a: In 2008 the institution was declared a Deemed to be University under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956.

q: What are the core values of the university?
a: The core values are Faith in God, Moral Uprightness, Love of Fellow Beings, Social Responsibility and Pursuit of Excellence.

q: How many weeks of teaching are there in a semester?
a: Each semester has 15 weeks of teaching, one week for the Mid Semester Examination and three weeks for the End Semester Examination.

q: What is the minimum duration of a PhD programme?
a: The minimum duration of a PhD programme is three years, including the course work.

q: How many undergraduate programmes are offered in 2026-27?
a: In 2026-27 the University offers 113 undergraduate, 83 postgraduate and 36 doctoral programmes.

q: Can I exit my UG programme after the first year?
a: Yes. You can exit after the first year with a UG Certificate, provided you complete the first-year requirements plus four credits for a vocational course, which may be fulfilled through a two-month internship.

q: How many multidisciplinary courses (MDC) must I complete?
a: Three MDCs of 3 credits each are required. Two must be completed before the end of the second semester, and one must be a 12-week SWAYAM course completed by the end of the fourth semester.

q: How many credits are given for Holistic Education?
a: Holistic Education carries four credits, one credit in each of the first four semesters. The value-added courses together carry a minimum of six credits.

q: What is the duration of the Mid Semester Examination?
a: The Mid Semester Examination is two hours long, for both regular and repeat examinations.

q: How soon must I raise corrections on my evaluated MSE answer script?
a: Corrections, if any, must be raised within 24 hours of receiving the evaluated script.

q: How many attendance marks do I get with 96% attendance?
a: Attendance of 95% to 100% earns 5 internal marks.

q: How many repeat MSE chances are allowed in a 3-year programme?
a: Three-year programmes allow 2 repeat chances (4/5-year programmes allow 3, and 2-year programmes allow 1).

q: How long is the End Semester Examination in the 50:50 pattern?
a: In the 50:50 pattern the ESE is conducted for 3 hours, evaluated out of 100 marks and converted to 50 marks.

q: What grade do I get for 70 to 79 percent?
a: A score of 70-79% earns an A+ grade, which is 9 points on the 10-point scale and 3.6 on the 4-point scale (Excellent).

q: How long does it take to get revaluation results?
a: Re-evaluation or re-totalling results are normally announced within one month from the last date of application.

q: Can I get a photocopy of my answer script?
a: Photocopies of answer scripts are not provided. At the COE's discretion, a student may view the answer script in the presence of the COE after paying the prescribed fee.
find: Photocopy of answer scripts shall not be provided

q: When are semester results announced?
a: Semester results are announced within 20 days from the date of the last examination and can be downloaded from the Student KP account.

q: How long is a CIA repeat tutorial?
a: A CIA repeat follows a 30-hour tutorial system completed within 30 days, with at most 2 hours of tutorial per day. Online sessions do not count.

q: When can I apply for a CIA repeat?
a: CIA repeat applications open twice a year and are notified in June and November on the University website.

q: Can a differently abled student bring a scribe?
a: Yes. Students who need a scribe must bring the scribe themselves and submit the scribe's details to the Office of Examinations in advance; requests should be made at least 2 weeks before the examination.

q: Is fee concession available for BTech or MBA students?
a: Fee concession is generally not available for self-financing programmes such as BTech and MBA, though exceptional cases may be considered.

q: Where is the Scholarship and Fellowship Support Cell located?
a: The SSC is in Room 206, Second Floor, Central Block, Bangalore Central Campus. Email: scholarship.support@christuniversity.in.

q: Can first-year students apply for internal scholarships?
a: No. First-year students are not eligible for internal scholarships.

q: How much is the sports excellence scholarship?
a: The sports excellence scholarship ranges from Rs 2,000 to Rs 10,000 per student, depending on the level of achievement (national, state or regional).

q: What documents must international students always carry?
a: International students must always carry a valid passport, a valid student visa and a valid residential permit; no international student may attend classes without all three.

q: What is Form C for international students?
a: If an international student lives in a PG or private apartment, the landlord must fill and submit Form C online; for students in University halls, the OIA handles Form C.

q: How many student council representatives does a class have?
a: A class with more than 40 students has 2 representatives (1 male, 1 female); a class of 40 or fewer has 1 representative.

q: What is the tenure of a student council member?
a: The normal tenure is one year, renewable through fresh nomination.

q: What is the dress code for students?
a: Male students wear formal trousers and shirts; female students wear salwar kameez with dupatta. T-shirts, cargo pants, sleeveless or tight attire are not permitted.

q: What happens if my phone is found in use in class?
a: Phones must be switched off in classrooms. Phones found in use may be confiscated and returned only upon completion of the course.

q: Will I get attendance if I come late to class?
a: Late-comers may be allowed in at the teacher's discretion but are not credited with attendance for that period.

q: How can my parents check my attendance?
a: Attendance-cum-progress reports are online at www.christuniversity.in/kp; parents can get login credentials by emailing ipm@christuniversity.in.

q: What is the maximum fine for ragging?
a: Punishments for ragging include a fine of up to Rs 1,00,000, rustication for up to 4 semesters, or expulsion.

q: Within how many days can I appeal an ICC decision?
a: An appeal to the Internal Complaints Appellate Committee must be received within 15 days of the ICC decision being communicated.

q: Which citation style should engineering students use?
a: Sciences and Engineering students use the IEEE Editorial Style Manual.

q: How early must an auditorium be booked?
a: Auditoriums must be booked at least one week in advance, with an HoD letter at the Block I Reception (Central Campus) or the campus office.
